evidence: Every declared server route reaches an authentication or authorization check somewhere in its call path
expected_output: One observation row per route with route, file, line, auth_reached, auth_symbol, path (the call chain as the artifact), path_resolution (exact|inferred)

assertions.description: Every declared route reaches an authentication check in its call path (recursive CTE over graph.db).

notes: Live as of M4: route nodes are extracted from the code (express-style registrations), and reaches(route, authCheck) is answered by recursive CTE over calls/handles edges. Auth detection is a name heuristic (default: /auth/i) — override with graph.authPatterns in rampscan.config.json. A repo with no detected routes stays honestly unevidenced, never vacuously evidenced. Empty-set discipline — Guard: the collector omits this recipe's observation key entirely when the graph found no route, because `count_eq 0` over zero rows would report full auth coverage for a repository that serves nothing.

plain.checks: Finds the HTTP routes the code registers, then follows each route's call path to see whether it reaches an authentication or authorization check.
plain.violation: A route serves requests with no identity check anywhere on the way in. Anyone who can reach the port can call it, whatever the documentation says about who is supposed to.
plain.fix: Add the check to the route's handler, or to middleware mounted in front of it. A route that is meant to be public — a health check, a login endpoint — still appears here, and the honest answer for it is a recorded decision saying so.
